'''Joséphine Guidy Wandja''' (born 1945, also '''Guidy-Wandja''') is an [[Ivory Coast|Ivorian]] mathematician.<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|id=Guidy-Wandja|title=Joséphine Guidy-Wandja}}</ref> She is the first African woman with a [[PhD]] in mathematics.

==Early life==

She moved to France aged 14.<ref name=Amina>{{cite web| url=http://aflit.arts.uwa.edu.au/AMINAGuidyWandja.html| archive-url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20160416184914/http://aflit.arts.uwa.edu.au/AMINAGuidyWandja.html| url-status=dead| title=Interview de Joséphine Guidy Wandja| publisher=Amina| date=July 1986| archive-date=16 April 2016| pages=50–53| accessdate=16 March 2019}}</ref> She attended the [[Lycée Jules-Ferry (Paris)|Lycée Jules-Ferry]] in Paris, and later the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].<ref name=Amina/> Her [[master's degree]] thesis was entitled ''Sous les courbes fermées convexes du plan et le théorème des quatre sommets'' (''Under closed convex curves in the plane and the theorem of four peaks'').<ref>{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FC9tAwAAQBAJ&q=Jos%C3%A9phine+Guidy+Wandja| title= History of Mathematics in Africa: 2000-2011| last1=Gerdes| first1=Paulus|author1-link=Paulus Gerdes| last2= Djebbar| first2= Ahmed| publisher=[[Lulu.com]]| date=2011| isbn= 9781105141003| access-date=16 March 2019}}</ref> Whilst working in Paris in the late 1960s she was advised by [[René Thom]], [[Henri Cartan]] and [[Paulette Libermann|Paulette Liberman]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://aflit.arts.uwa.edu.au/AMINAGuidyWandja.html|title=AMINA Guidy Wandja|website=aflit.arts.uwa.edu.au|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> She studied for a [[PhD]] at the [[University of Abidjan]], becoming the first African woman to get a [[PhD]] in mathematics.<ref name=AC>{{cite web| url= http://africultures.com/les-femmes-peinent-a-percer-les-bulles-7367/| title= Les femmes peinent à percer les bulles| language=fr| last= Cassiau-Haurie| first=Christophe| publisher=Africultures| date=20 February 2008| accessdate=16 March 2019}}</ref><ref name=CWM>{{cite web| url= https://www.mathunion.org/cwm/people/gallery/josephine-guidy-wandja| title= Joséphine Guidy-Wandja| publisher=Committee for Women in Mathematics| accessdate=16 March 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1969, she worked at the Lycée [[Jacques Amyot]] in [[Melun]], before working for a year at the [[Paris Diderot University]].<ref name=Amina/> In 1971, she joined the University of Abidjan.<ref name=Amina/> There she became the first African female university mathematics professor.<ref name=CWM/> In 1983, she was appointed the president of the International Committee on Mathematics in Developing Countries (ICOMIDC). The organisation was set up during the [[International Mathematical Union]] (IMU) [[Academic conference|conference]] in [[Warsaw]], Poland, but without the IMU's knowledge.<ref name= Lehto>{{cite book| url= https://books.google.com/books?id=YxTSBwAAQBAJ&q=Jos%C3%A9phine+Guidy+Wandja| title= Mathematics Without Borders: A History of the International Mathematical Union| last=Lehto| first=Olli| date= 6 December 2012| publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media]]| page=268| isbn= 9781461206132| access-date=16 March 2019}}</ref> In 1986, she wrote a humorous 24 page mathematical comic book ''Yao crack en maths''.<ref name=AC/><ref>{{cite news| url=http://news.abidjan.net/h/581959.html| title= Littérature pour enfant : "Yao crack en math", une bande dessinée qui démystifie les maths|language=fr| work=Abidijan.net| date=10 February 2016| accessdate=16 March 2018}}</ref> In 1985, she organised an ICOMIDC conference in [[Yamoussoukro]], Ivory Coast.<ref name=Lehto/>

She is an officer of the Ivorian Order of Merit of National Education, and the French [[Ordre des Palmes Académiques]].<ref name=Amina/><ref name=CWM/>
